reclamation.why: Three goods invoices were received by Redwood while insolvent within 45 days before the 2026-03-10 petition (window opens 2026-01-24): MS-7740 (rec. 2026-02-04, unpaid balance 25,600), MS-7788 (rec. 2026-02-20, 41,300), MS-7815 (rec. 2026-03-04, 36,800) — 103,700 of unpaid value on in-window goods (the 36,800 already paid on MS-7740 is not reclaimable). §546(c)(1) requires WRITTEN demand no later than 45 days after receipt; for MS-7740 that date (2026-03-21) falls after commencement, so the later 20-days-after-petition rule governs: demand must be served on or before 2026-03-30 (11 days from today). No demand appears in the file. CAVEATS: (a) reclamation is subject to the DIP lender's blanket lien (library note to bc_546c) so the reclamation right is likely of little or no real value — assert it to preserve leverage; (b) insolvency at each receipt is assumed from the chapter 11 filing, not yet proven (unlike §547, where the library states insolvency is presumed during the 90 days, the reclamation note states no presumption); (c) traceability of identifiable goods is a practical necessity but not addressed in the library — assumed, not in the file. MS-7701 (rec. 2026-01-14) is outside the 45-day window and was paid in full.

ordinary_course_defense.reasoning: 90-day window opens 2025-12-10. Insolvency during the window is presumed (library bc_547.md, §547(f)). Four payments: 2025-12-18 $51,000 (45 days after invoice, ACH) and 2026-01-22 $44,000 (43 days, ACH) continue the parties' PRE-WINDOW pattern — the six earlier payments (Apr-Nov 2025) were all 43-47 days after invoice, all ACH — and match each other — §547(c)(2)(A) protection (95,000); the Jan 22 payment came 2 days after the terms-change email but with unchanged speed and method, so it stays protected. 2026-02-10 $48,200 (29 days, ACH) and 2026-02-27 $36,800 (partial, WIRE) are EXPOSED (85,000): CLIENT ADMISSIONS (2026-03-19) confirm Mesa cut terms to net-15 in January, conditioned each new shipment on payment of the oldest open invoice, and made the 2/27 wire a shipping condition ('no steel until it hit our account') — the library states payments under shortened terms, pressure, or unusual methods (wire on demand) compared with the parties' history generally fall outside (c)(2)(A), and Mesa's own credit manager is the witness to the pressure. (c)(2)(B) 'ordinary business terms' (industry standard) untested — no industry evidence in file. Creditor bears the burden on (c) defenses, §547(g). Net effect: §547(c)(4) new value (unsecured, unpaid) is not limited to goods — after the 2/10 transfer Mesa gave 99,400 of unpaid new value (78,100 goods + 6,900 freight + 14,400 services), and after the 2/27 transfer it gave 51,200 (36,800 goods + 14,400 services); no payment was received after 2/27, so the 'otherwise unavoidable transfer' cutback does not apply (library bc_547.md). Each exposed transfer is covered by the new value given after it; goods alone would also cover (78,100 vs 48,200; exactly 36,800 vs 36,800). Net exposure ~0; worst case ~36,800 if a court holds new value given after the LAST transfer cannot offset that transfer — that sequencing rule is NOT in the library — labeled unverified.

stay_violations: 2026-03-12: 'FINAL NOTICE — pay $210,000 within 5 days or we refer to collections' letter, mailed and emailed — an act to collect a pre-petition claim, §362(a)(6) (library bc_362.md: dunning letters after petition are acts to collect).

2026-03-15: collection call to Redwood AP after the petition; AP told Mesa 'we filed Chapter 11, talk to counsel'; Mesa's AR clerk replied 'that's not our problem, you owe us' — continued collection attempt, and from this date Mesa had actual knowledge, making later violations willful under §362(k).

2026-03-18: email to Redwood CFO threatening to 'hold all future shipments and report to credit bureaus' — threats to report to credit bureaus after the petition are acts to collect (library bc_362.md); §362(k) liability for willful violations includes actual damages, costs and attorneys' fees, and punitive damages in appropriate circumstances; courts also sanction creditors for willful violations under §105 (library bc_362.md). The shipment-withholding threat is not squarely addressed in the library — flagged unverified.

[DATE UNKNOWN — client could not say] When Redwood's counsel offered continued supply on normal terms, Mesa (Frank) answered 'pay first': conditioning post-petition dealings on payment of pre-petition debt is a likely act to collect under §362(a)(6) ('any act to collect... a claim that arose before the commencement' — library bc_362.md), though this exact pattern is not squarely addressed in the library, so the characterization is flagged unverified. Independently, the refusal destroys critical-vendor eligibility: the vendor must agree to customary trade terms (library critical_vendor_practice.md).
